paper.title_en: From Hubble to Snap Parameters: A Gaussian Process Reconstruction
paper.abstract_en: By using recent $H(z)$ and SNe Ia data, we reconstruct the evolution of kinematic parameters $H(z)$, $q(z)$, jerk and snap, using a model-independent, non-parametric method, namely, the Gaussian Processes. Throughout the present analysis, we have allowed for a spatial curvature prior, based on Planck 18 constraints. In the case of SNe Ia, we modify a python package (GaPP) in order to obtain the reconstruction of the fourth derivative of a function, thereby allowing us to obtain the snap from comoving distances. Furthermore, using a method of importance sampling, we combine $H(z)$ and SNe Ia reconstructions in order to find joint constraints for the kinematic parameters. We find for the current values of the parameters: $H_0 =67.2 \pm 6.2$ km/s/Mpc, $q_0 = -0.54^{+0.06}_{-0.05}$, $j_0=0.94^{+0.20}_{-0.18}$, $s_0=-0.62^{+0.26}_{-0.25}$ at 1$σ$ c.l. We find that these reconstructions are compatible with the predictions from flat $Λ$CDM model, at least for 2$σ$ confidence intervals.
